chapter.title: When a station jams

cards.body: Picture your line once it runs on its own: 40 runs in a day, and one fails. Which station dropped the item? In most setups, n8n keeps a record of each trip down the belt, and the station that jammed shows up in red. **When one station jams, you find that station and fix it. You don't rebuild the line.**
cards.simpler: Picture your line once it runs on its own. It runs 40 times in a day, and one run fails. Which station dropped the item? In most setups, n8n keeps a record of each trip down the belt. The station that jammed shows up in red. **When one station jams, you find it and fix just that one.** You don't rebuild the whole line. It's like a flat tire: you change the tire, not the car.

cards.prompt: Say your form-to-Slack line is running on its own and ran 40 times yesterday. This morning, run 23 shows an error. What's your first move?

options.text: Delete the workflow and build it again, carefully this time
Open run 23 in the Executions list and look for the red node
Run the workflow again with a fresh test form

whyNot.a: That's rebuilding the whole line, not finding the jam: 39 runs worked, so most of it is fine.
whyNot.c: That's a new item on the belt, not the one that jammed: it may go through fine and hide the problem.

cards.reteach: In most setups, n8n saves the runs your line makes on its own, including the broken ones. The failed run shows exactly which station stopped and what it was holding. So you start there, not with a rebuild.

cards.title: Each trip is recorded
cards.body:
In most setups, n8n saves each run your workflow makes on its own as an *execution*, a record of one trip down the belt. The Executions list shows them, each with a time and a status: succeeded or error.

Open a failed one and you see your line frozen at the moment it jammed. **The node that failed is marked in red.** Click it to see the error message, n8n's note on what went wrong, plus the item it was holding.

It's like a plane's black box, minus the drama. It recorded the trip, so you don't have to guess.
cards.simpler: Usually, each time your workflow runs on its own, n8n saves a record of that one trip down the belt, called an *execution*. The Executions list shows them, with the time and whether each worked or hit an error. Open a failed one and you see your line stopped where it jammed. **The failed station, called a node, is marked in red.** Click it to see what went wrong and the item it held. It's like a plane's black box.

cards.title: Priya's lead line
cards.body: Priya's workflow takes a new website form, adds a row to Google Sheets, then posts in Slack. On Tuesday at 9:12, run 14 failed. In the Executions list the Slack node was red, with an error saying it couldn't find the channel. Her Slack node was set to post in #sales-leads, and over the weekend someone had deleted that channel and moved the team to a new one, #leads. Nobody told the robot. She picked #leads from the list in the Slack node, retried run 14 from the Executions list, and the message landed. That took two minutes, with no rebuild.
cards.simpler: Priya's workflow takes a new website form, adds a row to Google Sheets, then posts in Slack. On Tuesday at 9:12, run 14 failed. In Executions, the Slack station was red, with a note saying it couldn't find the channel. Her Slack station was set to post in #sales-leads. Over the weekend, someone deleted that channel and moved the team to a new one, #leads. Nobody told the robot. Priya picked #leads from the list in the Slack station and retried run 14 from Executions. The message landed. **Two minutes, no rebuild.**

cards.prompt: Your Google Sheets node has the sheet name typed in: 'Leads 2026'. Now it's red, and the error says it can't find that sheet. A colleague renamed it 'Leads' yesterday. What do you do?

options.text: Retry the failed run as it is, a few times
Point the Sheets node at 'Leads', then retry the failed run
Rebuild every node from the form onwards

whyNot.a: That's repeating the jam, not fixing it: nothing changed, so it fails the same way.
whyNot.c: That's rebuilding the line, not fixing the station: the form and the other nodes did their jobs.

cards.reteach: The red node tells you which station broke and why. Change that one station so the reason goes away (here, the sheet name), then send the same failed item through again.

cards.title: Hiccups versus real faults
cards.body:
Not every jam needs you. Sometimes an app is just slow for a second, like a door that sticks once. For that, open the node's Settings and switch on *Retry On Fail*, which makes n8n try that station again a few times before giving up.

Retry won't fix a wrong channel or a missing field. **A real fault fails the same way every time**, so retry just jams three times instead of once. For those, you fix the station.
cards.simpler: Sometimes an app is slow for a second, like a door that sticks once. For that, turn on *Retry On Fail* in the station's Settings, so n8n tries again a few times. Retry can't fix a wrong channel or a missing field. **A real fault fails the same way every time.** For those, you fix the station itself.

cards.body: Sam's Gmail node went red: no address to send to. He rebuilt that node three times, and it kept failing. The real fault was one station back, in an Edit Fields node that copies the form's 'Email' answer into a field called 'to' for Gmail. The form question had been renamed to 'Work email', so Edit Fields found no 'Email' and handed Gmail an empty 'to'. **Click the red node and read its input first**: if the item arrived broken, the fix belongs upstream, in an earlier station.
cards.simpler: Sam's Gmail station went red: it had no address to send to. He rebuilt that station three times, and it still failed. The real problem was one station earlier. There, an Edit Fields station copied the form's 'Email' answer into a field called 'to', for Gmail to use. But the form question had been renamed to 'Work email'. So Edit Fields found no 'Email', and Gmail got an empty 'to'. **Click the red station and read what it was handed first.** If the item arrived broken, fix the station before it.

cards.prompt: Run 52 failed. The Gmail node is red, and its input shows the email field arrived empty. Where does the fix go?

options.text: In the Gmail node: rewrite it until it works
One station earlier, where the email field should get filled
In the Gmail node's Settings: switch on Retry On Fail

whyNot.a: That's the station that showed the jam, not the one that caused it: Gmail can't send to an empty address.
whyNot.c: That's the fix for a hiccup, not a real fault: an empty field stays empty on every try.

cards.reteach: Red marks where the line stopped, not always why. Check what the red node was handed. If the item arrived broken, walk back one station and fix it there.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: When a run fails, open it in Executions, click the red node, and read both the error and what it was handed. **Fix that one station, or the one before it, then retry the same run.** Save Retry On Fail for apps that hiccup.
cards.simpler: When a run fails, open it in Executions and click the red station. Read the error, and read what the station was handed. **Fix that one station, or the one before it, then retry the same run.** Keep Retry On Fail for apps that sometimes get stuck for a moment.

cards.body:
Open n8n, click Executions, and open the latest run you see there. Click each node and look at what went in and what came out. Then open one node's Settings and find Retry On Fail.

Tomorrow: one switch, and your line runs while you're asleep.
cards.simpler: Open n8n, click Executions, and open the latest run you see there. Click each station, one at a time. For each one, **look at what went in and what came out**. It's like peeking inside each box on the belt. Then open one station's Settings and find the switch called Retry On Fail. Tomorrow: one switch, and your line runs while you sleep.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now find which node failed, read why, and fix it without rebuilding the workflow.

dubious_claims: Slack node with the channel 'typed in by name': current n8n Slack node versions offer From list / By ID / By URL, so a name-typed channel may only match older node versions
'Retried run 14 with the saved workflow': n8n 2.0 split saving from publishing, so the retry menu's wording and behaviour may have changed
'With its usual settings, n8n saves each run': true for live production runs, but whether manual test runs are saved depends on version and settings, so the claim is too broad

Logic gap: card 1 says the line already 'ran 40 times yesterday', but the closing teaser says the next chapter's switch is what makes it run 'while you're asleep'. That suggests it wasn't running on its own yet
'No recipient' as the Gmail node's error text looks made up; the real n8n message probably reads differently
repairedFrom.why: Card 6 crams three ideas into about 104 words: hiccups versus real faults, Retry On Fail, and a whole separate error-workflow feature that no exercise tests, so the chapter's one idea gets diluted.
repairedFrom.fix: Cut the error-workflow paragraph and save it for a later chapter, so card 6 only contrasts a sticky door (retry it) with a real fault (fix the station).
